item.title: Ray propagation of circularly polarized light in an inhomogeneous medium: the optical Magnus effect from Maxwell's equations
item.description: arXiv:2611.03914v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the ray propagation of circularly polarized light in an inhomogeneous, isotropic and lossless medium, including the first correction to geometrical optics, the optical Magnus (spin Hall) effect. Starting from Maxwell's equations and the eikonal expansion to first order in $1/k_0$, we show that the polarization is parallel transported along the ray, identify the Berry connection and curvature of the helicity states, and obtain a ray action in which the Berry phase appears as a correction to the optical path length. This action leads to a Hamiltonian in which the refractive index is evaluated at a position shifted by the Berry connection, $\mathcal H_\sigma(\mathbf r,\mathbf p)=|\mathbf p|-n(\mathbf r+\mathbf A_\sigma(\mathbf p)/k_0) \simeq|\mathbf p|-n(\mathbf r)-k_0^{-1}\boldsymbol\nabla n\cdot\mathbf A_\sigma(\mathbf p)$. In terms of the physical position, the equations of motion contain the Berry curvature as an anomalous velocity. We give the equivalent non-canonical bracket form, the gauge transformation, and the equivalent time-parametrized formulation with the Hamiltonian $\hbar\omega=\hbar c|\mathbf k|/n$, and we state the approximations involved. The resulting ray equations are compared with analytic and numerical results. A planar interface, the helical ray in a cylindrical medium and the exact conservation of angular momentum provide checks. The formulation is set up for numerical propagation of rays in a medium with a spatially varying refractive index.
item.dc:creator: Igor Kuzmenko, Y. B. Band

item.title: Contrast-Enhanced Nonlinear Imaging with Moir\'e Flatband Superlattices
item.description: arXiv:2611.03951v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlinear metasurfaces offer a compact platform for infrared-to-visible conversion and imaging, yet resonant enhancement is often accompanied by restricted angular acceptance, limiting the range of transverse spatial frequencies that can interact efficiently with the nonlinear modes. Here, we address this challenge using a one-dimensional photonic moir\'e superlattice supporting multiple quasi-flat bands in the near-infrared. These moir\'e modes combine strong near-field enhancement with broad momentum-space accessibility, enabling efficient third-harmonic generation (THG) while maintaining stable excitation over a large angular range. Experimentally, we observe strong THG emission near $467~\mathrm{nm}$ under broadband excitation from $ 1180$ to $ 2000~\mathrm {nm} $. We further employ the nonlinear moir\'e superlattice for infrared imaging by converting an infrared target into visible through the THG process. By encoding image information into displacement-dependent THG signals and decoding their spatial variations, we experimentally resolve weak features and internal textures with improved contrast compared with THG imaging using nonlinear films or conventional nonlinear metasurfaces. These results establish photonic moir\'e superlattices as a versatile platform combining efficient frequency conversion, broad angular acceptance, and mode-sensitive spatial encoding for high-contrast, label-free nonlinear imaging with enhanced feature discrimination.
item.dc:creator: Amin Zamani, Lihang Feng, Jianji Liu, Ze Zheng, Gabriel Sanderson, Mohsen Rahmani, Peilong Hong, Lei Xu

item.title: Reconfigurable multi-tone mmWave/THz generation powered by high-efficiency Kerr parametric oscillation
item.description: arXiv:2611.03997v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Broadband and simultaneously accessible multi-tone millimeter-wave (mmWave) and terahertz (THz) signals are attractive for multi-band wireless communication and spectroscopy applications, yet their generation remains constrained by electronic bandwidth limitations and inefficient optical frequency conversion. Here, we demonstrate reconfigurable photonic generation of multi-tone mmWave/THz signals with comb spacings of 100, 200, 300, and 400 GHz, using a strongly asymmetric dual-ring silicon-nitride (SiN) microresonator and a broadband spiral plasmonic photomixer. A localized avoided-mode crossing (AMX) introduced by an auxiliary ring supports a fixed optical parametric oscillation (OPO) mode pair over an extended pump-detuning range, consistent with passive compensation of detuning-dependent phase mismatch. This enables a maximum pump-to-generated-line conversion efficiency of 67.3 % with 25.06 dB of pump depletion across different pump wavelength selections. Direct photomixing of these optical states produces simultaneous multi-frequency tones spanning 100 to 900 GHz without intermediate optical amplification. The generated carriers are further characterized through down-converted spectra, frequency-noise power spectral density (PSD), and Allan deviation measurements, yielding a \b{eta}-separation linewidth of 26 kHz at an observation time of 0.1 s. Optical modulation offers high radiated power levels exceeding 2 mW at 100 GHz at a duty cycle of 1 %, while mitigating thermal breakdown in the photomixer. High optical conversion efficiency, reconfigurable and selectable comb spacings, and broadband multi-tone generation on a chip-scale platform provide a compact route toward reconfigurable multi-band mmWave/THz sources for wireless communication, spectroscopy, and sensing.
item.dc:creator: Dong IL Lee, Fanqi Shen, Wenzheng Liu, Xinghe Jiang, Anika Tabassum, Alwaleed Aldhafeeri, Manas Choure, Jasmine Lu, Mona Jarrahi, Chee Wei Wong

item.title: Asymptotic electromagnetic transition conditions for thin layers: the arithmetic-mean field and susceptibility hybridization
item.description: arXiv:2611.04324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective transition conditions that replace a thin polarizable layer by a zero-thickness sheet are commonly applied in electromagnetic models of two-dimensional (2D) materials and metasurfaces. These conditions usually take the arithmetic mean of the fields on either side as the polarizing field at the boundary, and characterize the layer by the $0^\mathrm{th}$ moment of its susceptibility, but both choices are typically imposed rather than derived. We derive transition conditions for a finite-thickness, in-plane homogeneous, in-plane isotropic layer with a general nonlocal susceptibility, using a single-scale asymptotic expansion in $\eta = l\max(k_0,q)$, where $l$ is the layer thickness, $k_0$ the free-space wavenumber and $q$ the in-plane wavenumber. The sheet limit must be taken after resumming the out-of-plane depolarizing field, as this ensures that the resulting sheet susceptibility is independent of the material thickness. The arithmetic mean then emerges as the leading-order polarizing field for general susceptibility profiles. Asymmetries in the layer profile modify the effective susceptibility appearing in the transition conditions, rather than altering the arithmetic-mean field prescription. If the spatial profile is not even in both out-of-plane coordinates, in-plane and out-of-plane response hybridize, turning the diagonal volumetric susceptibility into a $q$-dependent effective tensor surface susceptibility with off-diagonal components. Mirror symmetry alone does not remove this hybridization. Comparison with exact solutions for local and separable layers shows that the derived conditions remain accurate to $O(\eta)$ across propagating and evanescent excitations, whereas the standard sheet conditions fail once hybridization becomes appreciable.
item.dc:creator: Asbjorn Hansen

item.title: Reference-Beam-Assisted Perturbation-Resistant Imaging Through A Single Multimode Fiber
item.description: arXiv:2611.04427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimode fiber (MMF) imaging is highly sensitive to mechanical perturbations, which alter modal coupling and disrupt the speckle-to-target mapping. Here, we propose a reference-beam-assisted method for image reconstruction across multiple fiber configurations. An independent reference beam propagates through the same MMF as the imaging signal without target modulation, providing target-independent transmission-state information through its speckle patterns without requiring a separate configuration-sensing structure. A neural network jointly processes the signal and reference speckles to reconstruct target images. Experiments with MNIST and Fashion-MNIST across 10 fiber configurations demonstrate improved reconstruction quality, faster training convergence, and more accurate configuration identification. Further evaluation across 40 configurations confirms the reconstruction benefit of reference-beam assistance over a larger set of perturbed fiber states. These results provide a foundation for developing perturbation-adaptive MMF imaging systems for flexible endoscopy and minimally invasive optical diagnostics.
item.dc:creator: Bowen Sun, Maohan Li, Jingwei Luo, Zhuoren Wan, Zhaoyang Wen, Yuan Chen, Wending Huang, Zijian Wang, Ming Yan, Heping Zeng

item.title: Impedance-controlled Laser Dynamics in Near-Zero Index Media
item.description: arXiv:2611.04578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near-zero-index (NZI) media have been explored for controlling spontaneous emission, but their impact on stimulated emission and lasing properties remains unexplored within their different classes, i.e., epsilon-near-zero (ENZ), mu-near-zero (MNZ), or epsilon-and-mu-near-zero (EMNZ). Here, we show theoretically that lasing emission depends on the class of NZI medium and can be controlled through its impedance. The major difference, as compared to conventional laser media, arises from the incorporation of dispersive electric and magnetic properties in the derivation of the Maxwell Boch equations. In this framework, the analysis of laser rate equation reveals that the ENZ class, with high impedance, can reduce the lasing threshold through enhanced electric-field interaction. Numerical simulations further show that the NZI class also governs the spectral response: whereas ENZ and MNZ classes suffer from multimode emission, the EMNZ class preserves single-mode emission.
item.dc:creator: Adrien Debacq, Andrei V. Lavrinenko, Elizaveta Semenova, Olivier Deparis, Micha\"el Lobet

item.title: LIPS-PC: Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification
item.description: arXiv:2611.04780v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In single-pixel (ghost) imaging, known illumination patterns probe an object and a detector with no spatial resolution returns one number per pattern. Each measurement costs acquisition time and photons and, for ionizing probes, contributes to delivered dose. Motivated by automated radiographic defect screening, where a class label suffices, we introduce Learning Illumination Patterns for Single-Pixel Classification (LIPS-PC). The patterns are learned end-to-end while the measurement operator remains one fixed linear matrix, identical for every input. We parameterize it as a residual correction to a two-dimensional discrete cosine transform (2D-DCT), $D=D_{\mathrm{base}}+\Delta$, and jointly train the correction and a compact classifier using cross-entropy, without a reconstruction objective. This yields a task-driven linear embedding through optimization. We evaluate LIPS-PC numerically on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST under a controlled protocol, then on RIAWELC, a real industrial X-ray weld-radiograph dataset. Across five budgets, $M\in{8,16,32,64,128}$, corresponding to sampling ratios from below 1% to 12.5%, the learned operator outperforms the best tested fixed transform by 9-15 percentage points at $M=8$ on all three datasets. Its eight-measurement accuracy requires roughly 16-32 measurements with the best fixed transform, indicating a $2\times$ to $4\times$ saving at comparable accuracy. The advantage generally shrinks as $M$ increases, with a small reversal on RIAWELC at higher budgets. These results show that learning what to measure is especially valuable when measurements are scarce.
item.dc:creator: Tomer Porat, Talya Eden, Eliahu Cohen

item.title: Observation of pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals
item.description: arXiv:2611.04827v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photonic pseudospins enable selective excitation and routing of light, but perturbations that mix opposite pseudospins can induce backscattering in helical edge channels. Here, we experimentally demonstrate pseudospin-locked chiral edge transport in gyromagnetic photonic crystals, combining pseudospin selectivity with nonreciprocal unidirectional propagation. By jointly engineering lattice deformation and magnetic bias, we control dipolar-quadrupolar band inversions and construct interfaces supporting pseudospin-selective chiral channels. Microwave near-field and transmission measurements reveal a single chiral edge branch that is selectively excited by only one source handedness and exhibits pronounced nonreciprocal transport. Extending this mechanism to multidomain structures, we combine two pseudospin channels into a common waveguide, separate them into distinct outputs, and route them through intersecting interfaces. These configurations realize a nonreciprocal photonic pseudospin multiplexer and demultiplexer, together with a waveguide crossing exhibiting average measured crosstalk of -14.1 and -15.8 dB for its two input channels. Our results present an experimental route to integrating pseudospin-selective channel control with chiral edge transport, providing a foundation for nonreciprocal photonic networks that use pseudospin to organize and route multiple wave channels.
item.dc:creator: Chengle Fan, Kaizhou Shi, Xiang Xi, Zhen Gao

item.title: Generalized Lorentz Framework for Active Semiconductor Quantum Surface Plasmonics
item.description: arXiv:2611.04933v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nanostructured semiconductors provide an actively tunable platform for light-matter interactions across a broad spectral range. As feature sizes shrink to the deep nanoscale (~10 nm scale), nonclassical carrier dynamics and surface plasmonic responses become prominent, creating substantial challenges for a rigorous and efficient theoretical treatment. Here we develop a generalized Lorentz framework for quantum surface plasmonics in nanostructured semiconductors with arbitrary energymomentum dispersion relations. The framework enables efficient quantitative treatment of carrier nonlocality, carrier surface accumulation and depletion, and nonlocal damping in three-dimensional semiconductor nanostructures, under electrical tuning and across a wide range of doping densities. Building on this framework, we further establish a rigorous quasinormal-mode analysis that provides transparent physical insight into complex surface plasmonic responses of multiscale semiconductor structures. We demonstrate electrically controlled deep-nanoscale carrier accumulation and depletion in a semiconductor nanoantenna, leading to pronounced plasmonic-response modulation that can be interpreted in terms of eigenmode shifts, creation, and annihilation. By quantifying and linking complex nonclassical carrier dynamics with plasmonic eigenmodes, our work establishes a comprehensive quantitative framework for active semiconductor quantum surface plasmonics and will foster the convergence of electronics and photonics at the deep nanoscale.
item.dc:creator: Wancong Li, Qiang Zhou, Runzhi Zou, Zi He, Pu Zhang, Hongwei Han, Shuangchun Wen, Xue-Wen Chen

item.title: Pump quantization changes optimal measurements for quantum sensing
item.description: arXiv:2611.03943v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard analyses of quantum phase sensing often neglect the overhead of generating squeezed-light by treating the pump as an undepleted classical resource. Realistically, the pump is a quantum object that undergoes significant depletion and entangles with the produced squeezed light, raising the question of how the crossover from a classical to a quantum pump limits the quantum advantage in sensing. Contrary to prior analyses, we show that quantum advantage persists despite pump quantization, but depends critically on the nonlinear $(\chi^{(2)})$ source dynamics. In particular, we demonstrate that Heisenberg scaling emerges in the regime of strong pump depletion, rather than maximum signal squeezing. At maximum squeezing, the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for interferometric sensing of an unknown phase scales as $N^{3/2}$, where $N$ is the pump photon number, surpassing the shot-noise limit but establishing that squeezing itself is insufficient to attain Heisenberg scaling of $N^2$. At maximal pump depletion, where the signal flux is maximized, the QFI scales as $N^2$. In this regime, standard photon counting is suboptimal, while a joint nonlinear measurement of the entire pump-signal system is shown to achieve Heisenberg scaling. Our work shows that pump quantization changes both the optimal operating point and the measurement strategies required to preserve a realistic quantum advantage in phase estimation and, more broadly, many-body quantum dynamics.
item.dc:creator: S. A. Wadood, L. Bello, T. Ilias, J. W. Fleischer

item.title: Thermally enhanced magnon-phonon resonance in van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3
item.description: arXiv:2611.04229v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Strong coupling between collective excitations provides a route to controlling quantum states of matter, yet its evolution under thermal fluctuations remains poorly understood. In the van der Waals antiferromagnet FePS3, strong magnon-phonon coupling is established at low temperatures. At the same time, recent terahertz experiments revealed the counterintuitive stabilization of a long-lived metastable magnetic state with an exceedingly long lifetime of 5 msec at the antiferromagnetic transition, not at the base temperature. This was attributed to a strongly coupled spin-lattice scenario, challenging the conventional wisdom that increased magnetic and thermal fluctuations near TN should be detrimental to the coherent control of a metastable phase. Thus it requires an independent examination for correct understanding. Using high-field Raman spectroscopy, we systematically investigate the temperature evolution of magnon-phonon coupling in FePS3. We observe a pronounced avoided crossing between magnon and phonon modes across a wide range of temperatures and find that the coupling strength remains remarkably robust with increasing temperatures. The zero-field magnon-phonon detuning decreases progressively with warming, driving the system toward resonance and thereby enhancing their hybridization near the transition temperature. This anomalous thermal evolution provides the crucial key to understanding the unusual terahertz-driven states recently reported in FePS3. More broadly, our results highlight van der Waals magnets as a promising platform for strong coupling among collective excitations and for controlling magnetic states through light-matter interactions.
item.dc:creator: Kai-Xuan Zhang, Beom Hyun Kim, Seungbok Lee, Hao Li, Eugene Park, Heejun Yang, Feng Jin, Qingming Zhang, Je-Geun Park

item.title: A New Bound on Light-by-Light Scattering in the Low-Energy Regime
item.description: arXiv:2611.04531v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The superposition principle at the heart of optics states that electromagnetic fields do not interact in vacuum. This principle is not universal, instead electromagnetic fields couple weakly via quantum vacuum fluctuations. Striking consequences are light-by-light scattering and vacuum birefringence. Experimental results from colliding X-ray free-electron and optical high-intensity lasers combined with dark-field detection and polarimetry for background suppression are reported. This approach yields the most stringent bound for light-by-light scattering in the low-energy regime achieved to date -- improving upon previous experimental limits by ten orders of magnitude -- and paves the way for precision measurements.

item.title: Wavefront engineering with atomic Huygens' surfaces made simple
item.description: arXiv:2611.04538v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Atomic arrays provide a cooperative platform for light-mediated interactions in nonlocal metasurfaces which can operate in the quantum regime without nanofabricated optical elements or intrinsic material absorption. We present a minimal atomic implementation to harness wavefront engineering and create a near-ideal intrinsic atomic Huygens' surface. A simple bilayer square lattice with a two-atom unit cell, not limited to small lattice spacings, provides near-unity reflectionless transmission and a full $2\pi$ phase control of transmitted light without the localized site-dependent level shifts of previous proposals. This simplification is achieved through nonlocal radiative excitations that provide the familiar electric-dipole response with even radiation parity as well as an odd-parity radiation channel whose leading multipolar interpretation combines magnetic-dipole and electric-quadrupole contributions in atoms exhibiting only electric dipole transitions. This eliminates the need to simultaneously excite pure electric-dipole and magnetic-dipole responses with exactly matched radiation. We derive a two-mode model for this response and show that it accurately captures full coupled-dipole simulations near the optimal lattice spacings. Because of the wide applicability of coupled-dipole models, the relevance of our microscopic analysis extends beyond atomic physics to nanostructured metasurfaces. Moreover, the same platform also connects directly to established subradiance-protected single-photon storage protocols, suggesting a route toward combining wavefront engineering, storage, and retrieval in a simple atomic bilayer.
item.dc:creator: K. E. Ballantine, J. Ruostekoski

item.title: Nonlinearity-Induced Suppression of Dissipation in Bath-Coupled Floquet Topological Insulators
item.description: arXiv:2611.04752v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Topological insulators can host chiral, disorder-robust edge states that dissipate energy when coupled to an external bath. We show that nonlinear interactions enable all-optical control over edge-state dissipation in a laser-written Floquet topological insulator periodically coupled to a photonic bath. Although moderate nonlinearity enhances dissipation due to mode mixing, increasing the nonlinear strength to an optimal value dramatically suppresses dissipation by forming highly localized traveling edge solitons. These results establish engineered system-bath coupling and nonlinear interactions as a route to suppress dissipation of chiral topological edge transport.
item.dc:creator: Bhoomija Chaurasia, Sebabrata Mukherjee

item.title: Temporal stretching of single-photon pulses by intra-cavity frequency conversion
item.description: arXiv:2611.04771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spectral bandwidth and frequency mismatch between quantum light emitters and quantum components is a common problem in the realization of hybrid quantum information networks. Here we propose a simultaneous solution to both of these problems by using a free-space cavity with an embedded nonlinear crystal that, through frequency conversion, facilitates perfect coupling into a cavity mode. The slow leakage of the cavity effectively stretches the photon pulse, resulting in a much longer photon pulse at a different wavelength. We show that the amount of stretching is strictly limited by the finesse and length of the cavity. Including realistic internal losses in the cavity, we show that it is possible to stretch a photon by at least two orders of magnitude with high efficiency. The proposed setup can thus constitute a valuable addition to the toolbox of quantum information technologies.
item.dc:creator: Mathias L. H. Korsgaard, Eva M. Gonz\'alez-Ruiz, Anders S. S{\o}rensen

item.title: Synchronization in one-dimensional arrays of photon condensates
item.description: arXiv:2611.04989v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the synchronization of coupled photonic Bose-Einstein condensates in dye-filled microcavity arrays, subject to a potential gradient. We show that in the absence of noise the desynchronisation threshold is the result of a dynamical instability. For a two-site system, we analytically derive the maximal potential difference that allows for a synchronized solution as a function of the system parameters and find that it crucially depends on the thermalization rate. For systems with $N$ sites, we find a $N^{-3}$ power law scaling for the critical potential difference. When quantum fluctuations are included, stochastic phase slips broaden the sharp transitions, yet the phase velocity and first order spatial coherence still reliably identify the instability threshold.
item.dc:creator: Klaas Luyckx, Michiel Yzewyn, Michiel Wouters

item.title: Effect of high odrer dispersion on soliton interaction in coupled Kerr cavities
item.description: arXiv:2611.05305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the interaction of dissipative Kerr solitons in two nearly identical coherently driven, coupled microresonators in the presence of third-order dispersion (TOD). Using an asymptotic reduction of the coupled Lugiato--Lefever equations, we derive effective interaction equations governing the soliton separation and collective drift for weak intercavity coupling. TOD breaks the parity symmetry of the soliton profile and qualitatively modifies the effective interaction, leading to asymmetric interaction forces and multiple stable and unstable soliton clusters. The existence and stability of these clusters are controlled by the relative phase of the driving fields and the group-velocity mismatch between the resonators. In particular, an appropriate value of the group-velocity mismatch can give rise to multiple stable bound states, whereas deviations from this value trigger successive saddle-node bifurcations, ultimately leading to periodic soliton collisions. The analytical predictions are confirmed by numerical simulations of the full coupled system.
item.dc:creator: Andrei G. Vladimirov

item.title: Reading Why: Born-Measured Attention with Exact Word Evidence on Light and Qubits
item.description: arXiv:2611.05355v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When a language model answers, we can usually only estimate why. We build a transformer in which every step is a Born measurement - attention $|\langle q|k\rangle|^4$ normalised over each row, a measured product in place of the feed-forward nonlinearity, and a Born readout. With its denominators held at their values for the input, each class probability is a polynomial in the word amplitudes, so its integrated-gradient evidence is computed by a finite quadrature with no quadrature error: the words' contributions sum to the class probability above its no-information share, to $10^{-11}$ or better. On e-SNLI natural language inference, with about 98k parameters outside the embedding, the model reaches $76.98 \pm 0.17$% test accuracy, level with a softmax transformer of the same size ($76.62 \pm 0.36$%). Deleting the word its evidence ranks first changes the answer in 45% of test pairs, out of the 53% any single deletion can change, against 32% for the softmax model explained the same way and 40% by its attention x gradient. Attention can look more like the words annotators highlighted, yet accounts for the answer less well: deleting the word it ranks first changes the Born Transformer's answer in 32% of pairs. The same weights compile exactly to optoelectronic optics and to qubits, and a coherent attention layer becomes one circuit equal to the model (852 CNOTs on 23 qubits). On IBM's ibm_kingston, reading only the attention overlaps by Hadamard tests, the device gave the model's answers on two short test pairs and kept or changed them under deletion as the model does; the evidence itself did not yet survive the device, and we work out the shots and calibration that measuring it on hardware would need.
item.dc:creator: Teerawat Tongloy, Jiraporn Pongsopa, Rangsan Jomtarak

item.title: Valley polarization driven by two-color circular fields from a strong-field tunneling perspective
item.description: arXiv:2608.03242v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Valley polarization in hexagonal materials driven by the form of the lightwave and its orientation relative to the lattice, rather than solely by the helicity of the driver, has recently been demonstrated both theoretically and experimentally. This has extended valley control to the non-resonant, sub-cycle regime and to inversion-symmetric materials. One interpretation of this field-orientation-dependent valley polarization is that the laser-dressed, cycle-averaged band structure obtained from a Floquet-type approach is modified so as to lift the degeneracy between the valleys. Here, we derive a complementary explanation based on strong-field tunneling dynamics. We show that the effective valley gap at the dominant injection times depends on the orientation of the field relative to the lattice through the trigonal-warping term of the low-energy dispersion. We derive general expressions for co- and counter-rotating $\omega+N\omega$ fields and show that the leading orientation-dependent contribution survives the cycle average only for field configurations compatible with the threefold lattice symmetry, most notably counter-rotating $\omega+2\omega$ and co-rotating $\omega+4\omega$ fields.
item.dc:creator: Rui E. F. Silva, Olga Smirnova, Misha Ivanov, \'Alvaro Jim\'enez-Gal\'an

item.title: Phase-controlled super-modes in a `lossy' tri-waveguide coupled micro-ring resonator system
item.description: arXiv:2608.24523v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In coupled micro-ring resonator (MRR) systems, the coupling process plays a critical role in determining the optical response, yet models of these structures typically assume this process to be either lossless, or dissipative with either purely real or purely imaginary coupling rate, respectively. Dissipative coupling is contingent on having appropriately phase engineered structures with intricate coupling geometries, but systems exhibiting `lossy coupling', i.e., characterized by complex-valued coupling rates, have received comparatively little attention. In this work, we investigate the effect of such `lossy' coupling, by modelling the optical response of a tri-waveguide coupled MRR system, using Temporal Coupled-Mode Theory (TCMT). The `lossy' coupling occurs via a common bus waveguide, positioned between a pair of MRRs, leading to the emergence of a pair of intrinsic resonances, whose frequency and linewidth may be tailored by controlling the respective coupling rates from either MRR. We develop these ideas, and by connecting the input (driving) waveguides, using a 3dB y-splitter, demonstrate a novel, coherently driven, lossy-coupled MRR, which exhibits either an absorptive or transparent resonance peak on demand by phase-controlled super-modes.
item.dc:creator: Tianrui Li, Max Goodwin, Matthew P. Halsall, Iain F. Crowe

item.title: Advances in the Vacuum Magnetic Birefringence measurement using a pulsed Foil Coil
item.description: arXiv:2610.06043v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, in the framework of the {\it Bir\'efringence Magn\'etique du Vide} (BMV) experiment, we present our current apparatus in detail and we discuss its critical points. We also report the results obtained using specially designed pulsed coils called Foil Coils. Our novel measurement of the vacuum linear magnetic birefringence constant is $K_{VMB} < 1.7 \cdot 10^{-21}~\text{T}^{-2}$ at a confidence level of 68$\%$, which is an improvement with respect to our previous 2014 measurement.
item.dc:creator: Enzo Rodriguez Alvarez, Jonathan Agil, Julien Billette, J\'er\^ome B\'eard, R\'emy Battesti, Carlo Rizzo

item.title: Universality of Layered Programmable Decompositions by Fourier Absorption
item.description: arXiv:2510.19397v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Decomposing arbitrary unitary transformations into physically realizable operations is fundamental to quantum information, quantum control, and linear optics. Layered programmable architectures implement such transformations by alternating tunable phase masks with fixed mode mixers. However, establishing their universality at fixed depth remains challenging: we show that neither a sufficient parameter count nor successful synthesis of sampled targets guarantees global coverage. We prove that an architecture is universal exactly when every reachable transformation can absorb a diagnostic input Fourier multiport by reprogramming its phase masks. The associated Fourier absorption residual (FAR) requires no external target ensemble, vanishes exactly for universal architectures, and bounds worst-target synthesis error. For four-mode Fourier architectures, a permutation obstruction rules out universality with five masks, even under small unitary mixer perturbations, whereas a constructive factorization establishes universality with seven. Beyond exact universality, comparison with a universal reference of the same depth yields certified uniform approximation bounds in terms of unitary mixer errors. Finally, numerical simulations using a geodesic phase optimizer illustrate the distinction between Fourier absorption and direct target synthesis.
item.dc:creator: Javier \'Alvarez-Vizoso, David Barral

item.title: Plasma waveguides for high-intensity laser pulses
item.description: arXiv:2512.08690v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fundamental to many applications of laser pulses in science and technology is an extended interaction length with matter that significantly exceeds the distance over which the pulse would normally diffract and transversely spread. At low intensity, the interaction could simply be the linear refraction provided by a glass optical fiber to keep the pulse from spreading. At higher pulse intensities, however, the goal extends beyond diffraction-free pulse transport: an extended interaction length of high intensity light can give rise to bright secondary sources of photons and, at relativistic intensities, beams of high energy charged particles. Since these applications require laser intensities well above the threshold for ionization of atoms, new methods for overcoming pulse diffraction in a plasma have been developed. Chief among them are plasma waveguides -- optical fibers composed of plasma, with characteristic mode structure. This article reviews the methods and theory of plasma waveguides, highlighting the recent development of meter-scale plasma waveguides that have been instrumental to the laser acceleration of high-charge electron beams to energies ~10 GeV
item.dc:creator: J. E. Shrock, B. Miao, E. Rockafellow, H. M. Milchberg

item.title: Mechanisms governing photon-pair generation and emission directionality in quantum metasurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2606.26303v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Metasurfaces are emerging as a promising platform for photon-pair generation through spontaneous parametric down-conversion, thanks to their compactness, integrability, and intrinsic multifunctionality, which enables the engineering of complex quantum states. However, their full potential remains only partially exploited because the physical mechanisms governing key properties of the generated photon pairs, such as generation efficiency and emission directionality, are not yet fully understood. As a result, metasurface designs and experimental configurations are often optimized through trial-and-error procedures. Here, we theoretically investigate the main mechanisms that control photon-pair generation and detection by studying how different pump configurations and measurement geometries affect the generation efficiency, emission directionality, and collection efficiency of the emitted photon pairs. This framework allows us to interpret existing experimental results and to provide general guidelines for the design of metasurfaces and the choice of experimental configurations in future experiments. Finally, we show that substrate thickness and multilayer configurations represent additional degrees of freedom for quantum metasurface design and can be engineered to enhance the generation efficiency and control the emission directionality, providing a new route for the optimization of photon-pair sources based on metasurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Paniate, Ivano Ruo-Berchera, Francesco Monticone

item.title: On Optimal Measurement-State Preparation via Geometric Transport of the Squeezing Ellipse
item.description: arXiv:2607.28620v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Preparation of optimal measurement states is a key requirement in quantum metrology utilizing squeezed states. Besides positioning the mean state, such preparation requires proper alignment of the squeezing ellipse. We discuss a geometric framework that transforms an initially misaligned squeezed input into a measurement-optimal state in SU(2)-symmetric systems. Within this framework, the orientation of the squeezing ellipse constitutes an additional geometric degree of freedom and evolves as the mean state follows a controlled trajectory on the unit sphere. The resulting rotation of the ellipse depends on the chosen trajectory and is linked to the geometric phase through the evolution of the local basis. The discussed framework is applicable to different physical platforms admitting an effective SU(2) description. As a particular example, we consider polarization-squeezed light and outline a possible implementation using a continuously varying birefringent element.
item.dc:creator: Vsevolod Salakhutdinov, Nikolay Kalinin

item.title: Efficient detection of spectral cluster states
item.description: arXiv:2610.09745v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Multimode entangled states of light are key resources for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum information processing. Exploiting their full capabilities requires detection strategies that can efficiently and simultaneously access a large number of modes and their quantum correlations. Multimode optical parametric amplification (MOPA) provides a promising approach by amplifying multiple quadratures prior to detection, rendering the measurement robust against subsequent optical losses while enabling broadband operation. Here, we demonstrate the spectral multimode capability of MOPA by simultaneously characterizing a broadband 60-node dual-rail continuous-variable cluster state. We reconstruct the cluster-state nullifiers across the spectral modes and observe nearly uniform squeezing of up to -6.9 dB, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the highest level reported for pulsed spectrally multimode squeezed light. Furthermore, by evaluating the van Loock-Furusawa criterion across all relevant bipartitions, we verify genuine multipartite entanglement throughout the 60-node state. These results establish MOPA as a promising platform for scalable high-dimensional quantum information processing in the spectral domain.
item.dc:creator: M. Kalash, U. -N. Han, C. Roh, M. H. M. Passos, Y. -S. Ra, M. V. Chekhova

item.title: Seeing Why: Exact Evidence Maps for Quantum and Optical Image Classifiers
item.description: arXiv:2611.01993v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When an image classifier decides, we can usually only estimate why. For quantum and all-optical classifiers that act linearly on amplitude-encoded pictures up to the measurement, with no trained classical network before or after them, each class's Born probability above its no-information share, $P_g - b_g$, splits exactly into contributions of the encoded amplitudes, shown as Born evidence maps (BEM) over the picture. The split itself follows from known results on quadratic forms: with the transmitted light held fixed, it is what Integrated Gradients from a zero baseline and the Shapley value give. What we add is a way to measure it on the hardware that classifies, from class probabilities on a quantum chip or from camera frames on a lens bench, with no gradient circuit and no light sent backwards; a $g\times g$ map takes $1 + 2g^2$ runs. Deleting the 5% of pixels with the highest evidence drops accuracy from 73% to 9%, as occlusion does with 1,024 extra runs per picture, whereas gradient saliency removes much less. The classifiers share one architecture, a Fourier-plane mask followed by a brickwall circuit on qubits or by phase plates on a lens bench, read by a fixed Born headroom readout with no trained parameter; centring each picture on its own mean lets dark features count as much as bright ones. In simulation, four phase plates at a single wavelength reach 72.3% on Caltech-10 colour photographs. On IBM's ibm_kingston, with the mask applied before approximate loading, 300 test pictures were classified at 37.7% against 10% by chance (56.3% in exact simulation), and $2\times2$ maps of ten correctly classified pictures, one per class chosen by a stated rule, measured on the chip, agreed with the exact ones ($r = 0.77$). The maps also revealed a shortcut in the data; as the trim that removed it was chosen on test pictures, the Caltech-10 results are exploratory.
item.dc:creator: Teerawat Tongloy, Rangsan Jomtarak
